_note: Second reading of AI reader 112's anchors, part 1: opioid withdrawal (Gowing 2016, Gowing 2017, Sharma 2025).

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › 1. Alpha2-adrenergic agonists compared with placebo › (a) Withdrawal syndrome, 2nd paragraph
tasks.extracted: Severe withdrawal, alpha2 agonist (clonidine or lofexidine) against placebo: RR 0.32 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.57), 3 trials, 148 participants, GRADE moderate (downgraded for few events); illustrative 589 per 1000 with placebo against 188 per 1000. Leaving out the high-risk trial (Batey 1987): RR 0.28 (0.09 to 0.83), 117 participants.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › 1 › (d) Completion of treatment, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Completion of withdrawal treatment, alpha2 agonist against placebo: RR 1.95 (1.34 to 2.84), 3 trials, 148 participants, GRADE moderate; illustrative 288 per 1000 with placebo against 561 per 1000. Without Batey 1987: RR 2.12 (1.40 to 3.19), 117 participants.

tasks.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › 1 › (c) Adverse effects, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Sedation and dry mouth about twice as common with clonidine as with placebo (Benos 1985); drowsiness and dizziness in 7 of 16 on clonidine against 0 of 15 on placebo (Batey 1987); with lofexidine, blood pressure fell, hypotension 18% against 0% and insomnia 42% against 9%, and 4 of 35 against 0 of 33 stopped treatment for adverse effects (Yu 2008).

tasks.locator: Characteristics of included studies, Batey 1987, Benos 1985 and Yu 2008; Results › Description of studies › Participant characteristics, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: The pooled placebo trials are not named in the text; their group sizes (Batey 1987, 31, outpatient clinic, Australia; Benos 1985, 49, inpatient, Germany; Yu 2008, 68, inpatient, multiple US sites, terminated early for significant findings) add up to 148 (editors' arithmetic). Across the review, 19 of 26 trials involved withdrawal from heroin or other short-acting opioids; no trial is described as involving fentanyl.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › 2 › (a) Withdrawal syndrome › Intensity of withdrawal, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Against reducing doses of methadone: severe withdrawal RR 1.18 (0.81 to 1.73), 5 trials, 340 participants, GRADE low; peak withdrawal score SMD 0.22 (-0.02 to 0.46), 2 trials, 263, moderate; overall severity SMD 0.13 (-0.24 to 0.49), 3 trials, 119, moderate.

tasks.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › 2 › (a) Time course of withdrawal, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: In all eight trials that described the time course, withdrawal signs and symptoms appeared earlier and resolved sooner with an alpha2 agonist; with methadone, withdrawal peaked late, as the methadone was withdrawn.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › 2 › (b) Duration of treatment, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Time in treatment shorter with an alpha2 agonist: SMD -1.07 (-1.31 to -0.83), 3 trials, 310 participants, GRADE low; SMD -1.04 (-1.44 to -0.64) without the high-risk trial.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › 2 › (c) Nature and incidence of adverse effects, 1st, 2nd and 4th paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Hypotensive or other adverse effects RR 1.92 (1.19 to 3.10), 6 trials, 464 participants, GRADE low; illustrative 79 against 151 per 1000; without the three high-risk trials RR 2.02 (0.62 to 6.64), 203 participants. Drop-out for adverse effects RR 3.62 (0.77 to 16.94), 4 trials, 153 participants, no events in methadone arms. In one trial 89 of 100 people on clonidine had dizziness on standing.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › 2 › (d) Completion of treatment, 4th paragraph; Effect of opioid used; Effect of treatment setting
tasks.extracted: Completion RR 0.85 (0.69 to 1.05), 9 trials, 659 participants, GRADE low (selection bias, heterogeneity); illustrative 568 against 483 per 1000; without San 1990 RR 0.91 (0.75 to 1.11). Heroin RR 0.87 (0.61 to 1.25); methadone RR 0.97 (0.80 to 1.18); inpatient RR 0.87 (0.68 to 1.12), I2 67%; outpatient RR 1.09 (0.73 to 1.64).

tasks.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › 3. Clonidine compared to lofexidine or guanfacine › (d) Nature and incidence of adverse effects › Hypotension, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Postural hypotension in 8 of 14 on lofexidine against 13 of 14 on clonidine (Kahn 1997); doses withheld for low blood pressure on 4.1% of occasions with lofexidine against 8.9% with clonidine (Lin 1997); not pooled.

tasks.locator: Discussion › Summary of main results › 2. (a) Withdrawal syndrome experienced, 2nd paragraph; Potential biases in the review process, 3rd paragraph
tasks.extracted: Neither alpha2 agonists nor a methadone taper fully suppressed aches and pains, sleep disturbance, loss of energy, chills or anxiety. The authors note that fixed methadone tapers in blinded trials, unlike flexible tapers in practice, bias the comparison against methadone.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus alpha2-adrenergic agonists › Completion of treatment, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Completion of withdrawal treatment, buprenorphine against clonidine or lofexidine: RR 1.59 (95% CI 1.23 to 2.06), 11 trials (12 comparisons), 1264 participants, GRADE moderate (heterogeneity above 60%); illustrative 453 against 721 per 1000; number needed to treat for one additional completion 4 (2.8 to 6.7); inpatient RR 1.74 (1.05 to 2.89), 539 participants; outpatient RR 1.45 (1.12 to 1.88), 725 participants.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus alpha2-adrenergic agonists › Intensity of withdrawal, 3rd and 4th paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Mean overall withdrawal score lower with buprenorphine in all seven trials reporting it: SMD -0.43 (-0.58 to -0.28), 902 participants, GRADE moderate (blinding of subjective outcomes); without four high-risk trials SMD -0.37 (-0.58 to -0.16).

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus alpha2-adrenergic agonists › Duration of withdrawal treatment, 2nd paragraph
tasks.extracted: Time in treatment longer with buprenorphine: SMD 0.92 (0.57 to 1.27), 4 trials (5 comparisons), 558 participants, GRADE moderate; large in both inpatient and outpatient settings.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus alpha2-adrenergic agonists › Nature and incidence of adverse effects, 1st, 3rd and 8th paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Any adverse effect RR 0.93 (0.70 to 1.26), 3 trials (4 comparisons), 493 participants, GRADE very low; stopping for adverse effects only in clonidine arms, RR 0.20 (0.04 to 1.15), 3 inpatient trials, 134 participants, low. Dizziness, dry mouth and lethargy typical with clonidine; headache, constipation and nausea with buprenorphine.

tasks.locator: Results › Risk of bias in included studies › Other potential sources of bias, 2nd paragraph
tasks.extracted: Two trials (Collins 2005; Ling 2005) were stopped early because of clear benefit of one intervention, which the review notes could have introduced bias of uncertain size.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus tapered doses of methadone › Completion of treatment, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Completion, buprenorphine against methadone: RR 1.04 (0.91 to 1.20), 5 trials, 457 participants, GRADE moderate (fewer than 300 events); illustrative 528 per 1000 with methadone against 549 per 1000 (481 to 634) with buprenorphine.

tasks.locator: Summary of findings for the main comparison; Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus tapered doses of methadone › Duration of withdrawal treatment, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Mean days in treatment: MD 1.30 days (-8.11 to 10.72), 2 trials, 82 participants, GRADE low (different settings, small numbers).

tasks.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › Buprenorphine versus tapered doses of methadone › Intensity of withdrawal, 1st to 5th paragraphs; Nature and incidence of adverse effects, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: No meta-analysis of severity: Petitjean 2002 found no difference in total severity but higher scores on one day with buprenorphine and on two later days with methadone; Seifert 2002 found lower scores with buprenorphine on two assessment days; Bickel 1988 and Umbricht 2003 found no significant difference; two trials did not report severity. Three trials reported no significant adverse effects in either arm.

tasks.locator: Results › Description of studies › Treatment setting › Buprenorphine versus tapered doses of methadone, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Four of the six trials were inpatient (one in an AIDS service with admission for acute illness), one in a prison healthcare centre, and only one outpatient.

tasks.locator: Results › Self-Reported Withdrawal (SOWS) › Total Peak Scores, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Peak self-rated withdrawal differed by cohort, day and their interaction (F(1,6) = 12.44, p < 0.01): higher in the Fentanyl cohort from the second to the sixth stabilization day, with an inverted-U course that peaked on the second day and returned to the earlier cohort's level by the last day, while the Non-Fentanyl cohort declined steadily from the first day.

tasks.locator: Results › Self-Reported Withdrawal (SOWS) › Withdrawal Categorical Ratings, 1st paragraph; Individual Symptom Ratings, 1st paragraph; Table 2
tasks.extracted: Severe self-rated withdrawal in the Fentanyl against the Non-Fentanyl cohort: 48% against 16%, 47% against 8%, 37% against 6% and 27% against 6% on the second to fifth days; first and last days did not differ. Anxiety, sweating, tearing, runny nose, goosebumps, shaking, flushes, aches, restlessness, nausea, vomiting, twitching and stomach cramps all showed cohort, day and interaction effects; no single symptom drove the difference.

tasks.locator: Results › Observed Withdrawal (COWS) › Total Peak Scores, 1st paragraph; Withdrawal Categorical Ratings, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Peak observer-rated withdrawal higher in the Fentanyl cohort from the second to the seventh day (F(1,6) = 7.76, p < 0.001). No participant reached moderately severe or severe COWS scores; mild observer-rated withdrawal 73% against 33%, 70% against 13%, 73% against 18%, 60% against 15%, 53% against 18% and 40% against 14% on those days.

tasks.locator: Results › Physiological Measures › Heart Rate, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Tachycardia (heart rate above 100 at least once) in 43% of the Fentanyl cohort against 19% (p < 0.05); heart rate rose more steeply over the week in the Fentanyl cohort (interaction p = 0.007).

tasks.locator: Results › Participants, 1st paragraph; Table 1; Methods › Concomitant Medications, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: The Fentanyl cohort was older (mean 46.0, SD 10.1, against 41.2, SD 10.2; p = 0.021). Concomitant medicines for withdrawal symptoms were available during stabilization only in the Fentanyl trial, because of uncontrolled withdrawal.

tasks.locator: Discussion, 5th paragraph
tasks.extracted: The authors list as limitations the decade between cohorts, morphine possibly stabilizing people exposed to fentanyl poorly, incomplete urine confirmation in the earlier cohort, possible xylazine in the fentanyl supply, observers not necessarily blind to exposure, the small Fentanyl group, and possible nitazenes or other synthetic opioids.
